text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic during visit to Third army units in Pristina and Nis on Thursday called all leaders of Albanian parties for open talks to establish dialogue and find solution for disputed issues.
- Tobacco mafia empties state coffers. Serbia's budget in 1996 was 1.26 billion dinars short as only 7,000 tonnes of cigarettes was sold legally and 16,000 tonnes was sold on the black market.
- Serbs in Eastern Slavonia and West Srem in Croatia demand from U.N. transitional administration to secure necessary coniditions for elections scheduled for March 16.
- Bor mining and smelting complex targets $190 million exports in 1997.
- Unfair competition and insolvency are the main problems of trade organisations in Serbia, Chamber of commerce said.

- Serbian government proposed Ministry for economic and ownership transformation to be formed to replace ministry for private enterprise. The ministry is expected to draft ownership transformation law.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition leaders in Nis said protests would continue until all mandates are verified.
- Opposition leaders in Kragujevac said on Thursday state television and special police were the two main pillars of the present regime.
- Serbia's teachers continue strike while school directors employ refugees. About 70 percent of teachers not working.
- Fehmi Agani, vice president of Albanian party Democratic League of Kosova, said the issue of Kosovo can be solved only through dialogue with the authorities.
- Survey of the Centre for political and public opinion reasearch showed that 52 percent of Serbian citizens polled trust army the most.
- Economic experts say change of authorities is prerequisite for reforms in Serbia.

- Radoje Djukic, Serbian minister for private enterprise, said that negative social climate has been created towards private businesses. "There is pathological hatred towards it and is systematically destroyed," he said.

- Regime does not have the 2.4 billion dinars to pay late pensions but has paid half a billion dinars already to police "securing" protests, says Zoran Vacic, Serbian opposition Democratic party parliament member.
- Vojislav Seselj, Serbian radical party leader, said his party would vote against special law on recognition of part of local election results.
BORBA
- Kosovo is an inseparable part of Serbia and Yugoslavia, says Socialist Party of Serbia.
- Textile industry needs to import raw materials to revive production, currently running at 30 percent of capacities.

- Trial against Montenegrin opposition leader Novak Kilibarda on charges raised by Montenegro's president Momir Bulatovic for slandering republican leadership during election campaign beings in Niksic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Independent trade union of bank, insurance and other financial organizations' employees calls on court to establish legality of National Bank's decision on daily liquidity requirement for banks, which has closed down several banks.
- Pristina district court opens investigation against 16 Albanians arrested last month for activities towards Kosovo's secession from Serbia. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
